Text: Faculty have begun eating lunch in their cars.
Office hours have been replaced by an out-of-office message.
Three professors were seen updating their LinkedIn profiles during a faculty meeting.
The faculty senate reached quorum only after counting the portraits.
The faculty lounge coffee maker has been reassigned to a data center.
Requests for new forms now require a form.
The committee on committees has formed a subcommittee.
A student waited six hours to drop a class and is now enrolled in two more.
The org chart has been printed on a scroll.
Every decision now requires sign-off from a dean, a chatbot, and AI Corpone's legal team.
Lawyers have been spotted in the dining hall, eating for free.
The general counsel has stopped returning calls and started returning subpoenas.
Every campus email now ends with a 400-word disclaimer.
The campus bookstore now sells waivers in three sizes.
Nobody is sure which building is the library this week.
The bell tower has started ringing in binary.
Two different presidents gave this week's welcome address. Both were confident.
The campus map now includes a building labeled "probably."
Students have begun referring to the campus as "the facility."
The student newspaper is now printed entirely in complaints.
Tour guides walk backwards to keep an eye on the students.
The suggestion box has filed for emotional support.
